title: T3.4: Creates REST Services
description: Test your knowledge of REST service development in InterSystems IRIS

questions.question: Which class must your REST service class extend to create a REST service in InterSystems IRIS?
questions.explanation: REST services in InterSystems IRIS must extend %CSP.REST, which provides the foundation for handling HTTP requests and routing them to appropriate methods. %SOAP.WebService is for SOAP services, not REST. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: Which two of the following are valid approaches for defining REST service routes in InterSystems IRIS?

options.text: Using XData UrlMap block in the service class
Configuring routes in the iris.cpf file
Using the OpenAPI specification with spec-first approach
Defining routes in the Management Portal only

questions.explanation: REST routes can be defined using an XData UrlMap block in the code-first approach, or by importing an OpenAPI specification in the spec-first approach. Routes are not configured in iris.cpf or solely through the Management Portal. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GREST_intro

questions.question: In a REST service class, which XData block defines the routing configuration for HTTP requests?
questions.explanation: The XData UrlMap block defines the routing configuration, mapping URL patterns and HTTP methods to class methods. This block contains XML that specifies Routes and Maps for the REST service. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for defining a route in the XData UrlMap block that handles GET requests to retrieve a patient by ID?
questions.explanation: The correct syntax uses the Route element with Url attribute containing the path (with :id for parameters), Method for the HTTP verb, and Call for the method name to invoke. The colon notation (:id) indicates a URL parameter. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: Which HTTP methods are commonly used in RESTful services? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: RESTful services typically use GET (retrieve), POST (create), PUT (update), DELETE (remove), and OPTIONS (describe). CONNECT is used for proxying and is not typically part of REST API design. PATCH is also common for partial updates. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: In spec-first REST development, what is the primary file format used to define the REST API contract?
questions.explanation: InterSystems IRIS supports the OpenAPI Specification (OAS) format for spec-first REST development. You can import an OpenAPI specification to automatically generate REST service classes. WSDL is for SOAP services, not REST. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: What are the advantages of using the spec-first approach for REST service development? Select all that apply.

options.text: API contract is defined before implementation
Better collaboration between frontend and backend teams
No need to write any code

questions.explanation: Spec-first advantages include defining the contract upfront, automatic class generation, improved team collaboration, and automatic documentation. You still need to implement business logic, and performance depends on implementation quality. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: When using JWT (JSON Web Token) authentication for a REST service, which two classes must you configure to enable this authentication method?

options.text: OAuth/OpenID Connect client configuration and the dispatch class
The implementation (.impl) class and the specification (.spec) class
OAuth/OpenID Connect client configuration and the specification (.spec) class
The dispatch class and CSP application security settings

questions.explanation: To enable JWT authentication, you must configure the OAuth/OpenID Connect client configuration in the system and update the specification (.spec) class to reference this authentication method. The .impl class contains business logic, not security configuration. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GREST_securing

questions.question: What parameter must be set to 1 in a REST service class to enable CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)?
questions.explanation: Setting 'Parameter HandleCorsRequest = 1;' enables CORS support in the REST service class. This allows the service to handle preflight OPTIONS requests and add appropriate CORS headers to responses for cross-origin requests. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: Which of the following are valid authentication methods for securing REST services in InterSystems IRIS?
questions.explanation: InterSystems IRIS REST services support Basic Authentication, JWT, OAuth 2.0, and Kerberos authentication methods through CSP application configuration and OAuth/OpenID Connect integration. API Key and certificate-based authentication require custom implementation. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GREST_securing

questions.question: In the Management Portal, where do you configure the authentication method for a REST service application?

options.text: System Administration > Security > Applications > Web Applications

questions.explanation: REST service authentication is configured in the Web Applications settings under System Administration > Security > Applications > Web Applications. Here you specify the CSP application path, authentication method, and required security settings. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GREST_securing

questions.question: What is the purpose of the %request object in a REST service method?

options.text: To access HTTP request data including headers, parameters, and body

questions.explanation: The %request object provides access to all incoming HTTP request data including headers, query parameters, URL parameters, and the request body. It is automatically available in REST service methods for processing client requests. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: Which method should you call to return a JSON response from a REST service method?
questions.explanation: The inherited method WriteJSON() is used to serialize objects or dynamic objects to JSON and write them to the HTTP response stream with the correct content-type header. This is the standard pattern for returning JSON data from REST endpoints. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: What features does the InterSystems API Manager provide for REST services? Select all that apply.

options.text: Real-time monitoring of API calls and performance

questions.explanation: API Manager provides monitoring, rate limiting, analytics/reporting, and a developer portal. Code generation is handled by the OpenAPI import feature in IRIS itself, and database migration is not an API Manager function. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GIKNOW

questions.question: When documenting a REST service using OpenAPI, which section defines the data structures used in requests and responses?
questions.explanation: In OpenAPI 3.x, the components/schemas section defines reusable data structures (schemas) for request and response bodies. In OpenAPI 2.0 (Swagger), this was called 'definitions'. These schemas use JSON Schema format. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: What HTTP status code should a REST endpoint return when a resource is successfully created?
questions.explanation: HTTP status code 201 Created indicates that a new resource was successfully created. The response should typically include a Location header with the URI of the new resource. 200 OK is for successful GET/PUT, 204 for successful DELETE. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: Which of the following are best practices for REST API design in InterSystems IRIS?

options.text: Use nouns for resource names (e.g., /patients, not /getPatients)
Use HTTP methods to indicate operations (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
Include version number in the URL (e.g., /api/v1/patients)
Always return XML format for compatibility
Include authentication tokens in URL query parameters

questions.explanation: REST best practices include using nouns for resources, HTTP methods for operations, API versioning, and meaningful status codes. JSON is the standard format (not XML), and authentication tokens should be in headers (Authorization), not URL parameters for security. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GREST_intro

questions.question: In the XData UrlMap, what does the Forward attribute in a Map element do?

options.text: Forwards the request to another server
Delegates handling to another REST class
Enables request forwarding through a proxy

questions.explanation: The Forward attribute in a Map element delegates request handling to another REST service class. This allows you to organize large APIs by splitting functionality across multiple classes while maintaining a unified URL structure. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: How do you access a URL parameter defined as '/patient/:id' within the REST service method?

options.text: pId parameter in the method signature

questions.explanation: URL parameters defined with colon notation (:id) are automatically passed as method parameters with a 'p' prefix. So ':id' becomes the 'pId' parameter in the method signature: Method GetPatient(pId As %String). Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: What is the recommended way to handle errors and return appropriate error messages in a REST service?

options.text: Always return HTTP 200 with error details in the response body
Set HTTP status code appropriately and return error details in JSON format
Throw an exception and let IRIS handle it automatically

questions.explanation: Best practice is to set an appropriate HTTP status code (4xx for client errors, 5xx for server errors) and return error details in a consistent JSON structure. Use %response.Status to set the status code and return structured error information. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: When importing an OpenAPI specification into InterSystems IRIS, which type of class is automatically generated?

options.text: A single combined REST service class

questions.explanation: Importing an OpenAPI specification generates both a .spec class (containing the API contract and routing) and a .impl class (containing method stubs for implementation). The .spec class should not be modified as it's regenerated from the specification. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: Which of the following are valid content types for REST service requests and responses in InterSystems IRIS?
questions.explanation: InterSystems IRIS REST services can handle all these content types. JSON and XML are most common for APIs, text/plain for simple responses, multipart/form-data for file uploads, application/x-www-form-urlencoded for form submissions, and application/octet-stream for binary data. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: What is the purpose of the OnPreDispatch() method in a REST service class?

options.text: To validate the request before routing to the appropriate handler method
To generate the response after the handler method completes

questions.explanation: OnPreDispatch() is called before dispatching the request to the handler method. It's commonly used for authentication, request validation, logging, or setting up resources needed by handler methods. Return 1 to continue, 0 to halt processing. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSOAP_intro

questions.question: In API Manager, what is the primary purpose of defining a Service?

options.text: To create the REST service implementation code
To group and expose one or more REST APIs through a common endpoint

questions.explanation: In API Manager, a Service groups one or more REST APIs (Routes) and exposes them through a managed endpoint. Services provide centralized control for monitoring, rate limiting, authentication, and analytics across multiple APIs. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GIKNOW

questions.question: When implementing OAuth 2.0 authentication for a REST service, which components are required? Select all that apply.

options.text: Resource Server configuration in the REST service

questions.explanation: OAuth 2.0 implementation requires an Authorization Server (may be external like Azure AD), Client configuration in IRIS, Resource Server settings in the REST service to validate tokens, and SSL/TLS for secure token transmission. Tokens are typically stored in memory or cache, not SQL databases. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=ROARS_iam_oauth
